- display-type (the heading typeface): IBM Plex Sans. Shown with the reason: Made for code and open-source docs, so headings feel native next to your SDK and GitHub pages. Pairs cleanly with a monospace for metrics and process names.
- body-type (the body typeface): Libre Baskerville
- type-scale (type size and weight): 18px body, headings ×1.2
- brand-color (the brand colour): #38bdf8. Shown with the reason: Reads like a live data stream on a monitoring dashboard. Clearly apart from your green, amber and red status colours, so a button never looks like a warning or a failure.
- secondary-color (a supporting colour): None. Shown with the reason: Keep it to the brand colour and greys.
- accent-color (an accent colour): #8b5cf6. Shown with the reason: Mark the AI investigator's root-cause note with it, so the plain-language finding reads as its own thing on the dark page, apart from the sky-blue brand.
- neutral (the greys): Cool
- semantics (success/warning/error colours): #3fb950, #d29922, #f85149
- spacing (density and spacing): Tight, 4px base. Shown with the reason: Argus watches metrics, containers and processes at the same time. A 4px base keeps rows, labels and values close, so more of that data fits on screen before you scroll.
- radius (corner rounding): Soft, 8px. Shown with the reason: Corners line up with your 4px spacing grid. Buttons and cards look tight and technical, not harsh, and stay steady as people scan the page.
- depth (shadows and depth): Subtle

reply.summary: Your foundation is built for a dark monitoring dashboard: cool greys and quiet shadows keep the page calm, while sky-blue and violet carry meaning. IBM Plex Sans headings sit naturally next to your SDK, docs and GitHub pages, and tight 4px spacing fits more metrics, containers and processes on screen before anyone scrolls. It reads as serious open-source infrastructure, not a marketing site.
reply.rule: The brand colour #38bdf8 marks actions and live data on top of the cool greys, #8b5cf6 is saved only for the AI investigator's root-cause note, and #3fb950, #d29922 and #f85149 appear only as success, warning and error status.

reasons.surface: Dark matches the terminal and dashboard context where Argus runs, and keeps dense metric text easy to scan for long stretches without glare.
reasons.display-type: IBM Plex Sans was made for code and open-source docs, so headings feel native beside your SDK and GitHub pages and pair cleanly with a monospace for metric names.
reasons.body-type: Libre Baskerville is a serif, a font with small strokes at the ends of letters; it gives the AI's plain-language root-cause notes a steady, readable feel on the dark page.
reasons.type-scale: An 18px body is comfortable to read, and headings only 1.2x larger keep the hierarchy calm, so the page stays about your data rather than big marketing headlines.
reasons.brand-color: A live sky-blue reads like a streaming monitoring dashboard, and it sits clearly apart from your green, amber and red, so a button never looks like a warning or a failure.
reasons.secondary-color: Dropping a second support colour keeps attention on one action colour plus greys, so nothing competes with the brand or with status.
reasons.accent-color: Violet marks the AI investigator's root-cause note, so the plain-language finding reads as its own thing on the dark page, apart from the sky-blue brand.
reasons.neutral: Cool greys carry a slight blue tint that sits well with the sky-blue brand and reads as technical rather than warm or soft.
reasons.semantics: These green, amber and red values are the only colours used for status, so success, warning and error stay instantly recognisable and never blend into the brand.
reasons.spacing: Argus watches metrics, containers and processes at once; a 4px base keeps rows, labels and values close so more of that data fits on screen before you scroll.
reasons.radius: An 8px corner lines up with the 4px spacing grid, so buttons and cards look tight and technical rather than harsh, and stay steady as people scan the page.
reasons.depth: Subtle shadows lift cards and panels off the dark background just enough to show layers, without glow or clutter that would pull focus from the data.

description: Argus is an open-source monitoring tool for servers and applications, with an AI investigator built in. You run it on your own infrastructure with one Docker command, then add its SDK to your apps. It watches metrics, containers and processes, and when something looks wrong it investigates: it correlates metrics, logs and events and explains the likely root cause in plain language. Free and MIT licensed; your data never leaves your servers. The landing page should send people to the GitHub repo and the docs.
